name: Burkina Faso
summary: Red over green with a yellow five-pointed star in the centre. It was introduced in 1984 by Thomas Sankara, who renamed the country from Upper Volta to Burkina Faso, 'land of upright people'.
origin: Upper Volta's flag, from 1959, had black, white and red horizontal bands representing the three branches of the Volta River.
Captain Thomas Sankara came to power in 1983. On 4 August 1984, the first anniversary of his revolution, he changed the country's name and introduced the new flag in Pan-African colours.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The revolution and the struggle for liberation.

symbols.name: Yellow star
symbols.description: A five-pointed star in the centre.
symbols.meaning: The guiding light of the revolution.

facts: The country's name combines words from Mooré and Dyula meaning 'land of upright (honest) people'.
Sankara is credited with writing the national anthem, 'Une Seule Nuit'.
clues: Red over green with a yellow star in the centre.
Introduced in 1984 with a new country name meaning 'land of upright people'.
Its predecessor had three bands for three branches of a river.
